Check that no few contributors dominate a sum

check_dominance.Rd

Applies two rules from the Eurostat guidelines for output checking to every group:

  • (n, k) rule: the n largest contributors may not make up more than k of the total (default: 2 contributors, 85 %).

  • p % rule: the total minus the two largest contributions must be at least p of the largest, so the second largest contributor cannot estimate the largest within p. Groups with fewer than 3 contributors always fail this rule.

Usage

check_dominance(x, value, by = NULL, id = NULL, config = NULL, target = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame, or a table/matrix of counts.

value

Numeric variable that is summed.

by

Grouping variables. For an aggregated table the default is all non-numeric columns.

id

Contributor identifier. Contributions are summed per contributor first. Without id each row is one contributor.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

target

Label used in reports.

Value

A mimic_check. details lists failing groups and the rule they break.

Details

Use it before releasing sums, means or totals of skewed variables such as income, costs or catch.

See also

Other checks: check_differencing(), check_extremes(), check_group_disclosure(), check_k_anonymity(), check_keys(), check_min_count(), check_model(), check_suppression()

Examples

check_dominance(fake_persons, value = "income", by = "settlement",
                id = "person_id")
#> ✖ dominance (fake_persons): 3 of 22 groups of income are dominated by few contributors (n = 2, k = 0.85) and p = 0.1.
#>     settlement    rule_broken
#>  Settlement_19 (n, k) and p %
#>  Settlement_18 (n, k) and p %
#>  Settlement_20 (n, k) and p %
